  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports a quantitative comparison of radiation carcinogenesis between humans and mice using a mathematical model, providing a concordance statistic (time shift per dose).",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "Mouse models are vital for assessing risk from environmental carcinogens, including ionizing radiation, yet the interspecies difference in the dose response precludes direct application of experimental evidence to humans.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "oncology",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Herein, we take a mathematical approach to delineate the mechanism underlying the human-mouse difference in radiation-related cancer risk.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "We used a multistage carcinogenesis model assuming a mutational action of radiation to analyze previous data on cancer mortality in the Japanese atomic bomb survivors and in lifespan mouse experiments.",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "We used a multistage carcinogenesis model assuming a mutational action of radiation to analyze previous data on cancer mortality in the Japanese atomic bomb survivors and in lifespan mouse experiments.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The time shift per dose was larger by two orders of magnitude in humans (7.8 and 0.046 years per Gy for humans and mice, respectively, when exposed at ~35% of their lifetime)."
